stand: Round 3 running · audio workstream in parallel · 6 pieces won

stuecke.titel: 3 · Projectile as head with tail
stuecke.luecke: Head 8 px, tail 104 px, every wedge extension hits its module.

stuecke.titel: 1 · Damage numbers above the field
stuecke.luecke: Crits now carry an outline for as long as they live: contrast 19.0:1 instead of 3.38:1. Exactly two numbers in the frame are fully opaque, measured by 78 pure-white pixels in two clusters.

stuecke.titel: 5 · Range ring as a dark zone
stuecke.luecke: The cyan hairline has become a neutral-colored zone — the rule "neutral = geometry, saturated = ability" now applies to us too.

stuecke.titel: 6 · Hit feedback and layer order
stuecke.luecke: The kill effect sits above the living crowd instead of behind it, the impact glows, the enemy that was hit brightens.

stuecke.titel: 8 · Resource bar in all five sections
stuecke.luecke: The same bar now appears pixel-identical in base, combat, upgrades, prestige and settings.

stuecke.titel: 10 · The first hint
stuecke.luecke: The first sentence is "Move the mouse over coins", the sequence is monotonic. The timeout for the lingering note is still missing — round 3.

stuecke.titel: 7 · Health bars above all layers
stuecke.luecke: Unified, but the loop still sits in drawEnemies — ten layers paint over it afterwards. One runner bar had 0 of 54 correct pixels.

stuecke.titel: 11 · The crowd has no weight
stuecke.luecke: 20 px across and 122 glowing pixels per enemy versus 34 px and 454 for the benchmark. 4.63% pink area in the circle instead of 22.44%.

stuecke.titel: 12 · The grid shows through the tail
stuecke.luecke: The wedge is drawn with source-over at opacity 0.5 — the grid lines show through and break the monotonic falloff by up to 25 luminance units.

stuecke.titel: 4 · Upgrade tile: the calculation assumes three groups
stuecke.luecke: The Station group has four tiles once helper.collector is bought. On 86% of all window widths the tile drops below its own minimum — and the guard that is supposed to prevent this does not see the case.

stuecke.titel: 9 · Inventory as a dense tile grid
stuecke.luecke: Single-column row list in 232 px — twenty towers means twenty rows of scrolling. The benchmark fits the same into five columns with an overlapping tier badge.

stuecke.titel: 13 · Five icons without a single word
stuecke.luecke: The nav buttons only have title and aria-label. Behind one of them lies the game's only building guide. Plus three finished lock explanations that appear nowhere.

stuecke.titel: 14 · The lingering note has no timeout
stuecke.luecke: Anyone who never clicks "Got it" permanently sees 1 of 8 hints — measured over 55 hours of simulated play time. And the fuzz test cannot see it, because every simulated player clicks.

stuecke.titel: 15 · Nowhere does it say what the game is about
stuecke.luecke: No text names the goal or the loss condition. Three free starter modules sit in the inventory, and nothing says "you have towers, build them".

stuecke.titel: 16 · Boss without warning, defeat without explanation
stuecke.luecke: hint.boss only fires once the boss is already on the field. And a lost run costs nothing — the screen just says DEFEAT.

stuecke.titel: K1 · Three buses, real sliders, one limiter
stuecke.luecke: One slider with four steps, master is a bare GainNode. A boss death during a firefight adds up unchecked.

stuecke.titel: K2 · The 25 silent events
stuecke.luecke: 45 events, 20 listeners. All UI sound is silent.

stuecke.titel: K3 · There is no music at all
stuecke.luecke: Zero hits for musik/music/bgm/ambient in the source tree. Will be synthesized with Web Audio.

stuecke.titel: K4 · Sound without position and without tempo
stuecke.luecke: enemy.killed carries x/y, the listener throws it away. And at x4 the picture thins out, the sound does not.

stuecke.titel: 17 · Silver reads like geometry
stuecke.luecke: The silver coin measures rgb(163,167,194), chroma 31 — almost neutral. In the benchmark, currency has exactly one hue that appears nowhere else; neutral colors are reserved there for permanent geometry.

stuecke.titel: T1 · The crowd is computed quadratically
stuecke.luecke: stepCrowd checks every pair: 19,900 per tick with 200 enemies, at ×4 about 4.8 million distance calculations per second.

stuecke.titel: T2 · Work done every frame
stuecke.luecke: The HUD signature serializes the whole upgrade table every frame, and the developer bar builds its string even without ?debug.

stuecke.titel: T3 · The effect pools are too small
stuecke.luecke: 16 shockwaves and 72 fragments with up to 200 enemies: every new death overwrites a running decay.

log.text: Eight agents measured the benchmark and the code frame by frame and cut ten pieces.
Built the still-frame tool: deterministic wave, one frame, PNG to disk.
Round 1 (17 agents): projectile and first hint won, three failed.
Built the stress case pulk:200 — 194 enemies. New piece: the crowd has no weight.
Round 2 (23 agents): damage numbers, range ring, hit feedback and resource bar won.
Audio workstream started — it does not touch any file of the other workstreams.
Alarm checked: the critic measured 15 ms per frame. Our own measurement, three times: 0.78 to 1.3 ms. It was machine load from 23 simultaneous agents, not a regression in the code.
Round 3 (19 agents) started: four open pieces plus first minute, inventory and navigation.
Built the pixel reader tools/pixel.mjs: reads PNGs without a browser and without a third-party package, so re-measuring does not tie up the tab.
Found a bug in our own tool: still frames started before the image files had loaded — the same coin once as a gold fallback disc, once as a silver image. Fixed; two runs are now byte-identical.
